q: The flow of electrons from a place of lower potential to a place of higher potential is called an _____.
e: Electron flow is from low potential to high potential. That flow of charge is an electric current. The flow of electrons from a place of lower potential to a place of higher potential is called an electric current. Electric field or potential difference is not this quantity.

q: The rate of flow of electric charge through a cross-sectional area of a conductor is called an _____.
e: Electric current is charge passing a cross-section per second, I = Q/t. The rate of flow of electric charge through a cross-sectional area of a conductor is called an electric current. Electric field or electromotive force is not this quantity.

q: The amount of charge passing through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in one second is called an _____.
e: Electric current is charge passing a cross-section per second, I = Q/t. The amount of charge passing through a cross-sectional area of a conductor in one second is called an electric current. Voltage or resistance is not this quantity.

q: The mathematical formula for electric current is _____.
e: The defining equation is I = Q/t. The mathematical formula for electric current is I = (Q)/(t). I = (V)/(R) or Q = It is a different relation from I = (Q)/(t).

q: If $n$ electrons pass through a cross-sectional area of a conductor, the total amount of charge $Q$ is _____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. If n electrons pass through a cross-sectional area of a conductor, the total amount of charge Q is Q = ne. Q = (n)/(e) or Q = (e)/(n) is a different relation from Q = ne.

q: In the SI system, the unit of electric current is the _____.
e: SI current is the ampere. In the SI system, the unit of electric current is the ampere. Coulomb or volt is not this quantity.

q: One ampere is equivalent to _____.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. One ampere is equivalent to 1 C s^-1. 1 c s or 1 s c^-1 is not this quantity.

q: One milliampere (mA) is equal to _____.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. One milliampere (mA) is equal to 10^-3 A. Do not trade 10^-3 A for 10^-2 A or 10^-4 A.

q: One microampere ($\mu$A) is equal to _____.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. One microampere (μA) is equal to 10^-6 A. 10^-5 a or 10^-9 a is not this quantity.

q: The direction of current is conventionally defined as the direction of the flow of _____ charge from a higher potential to a lower potential.
e: Conventional current follows positive charge from high potential to low. Electron flow is the opposite arrow. The direction of current is conventionally defined as the direction of the flow of positive charge from a higher potential to a lower potential. Negative or neutral is not this quantity.

q: The direction of conventional current is _____ to that of the flow of electrons.
e: The direction of conventional current is opposite to that of the flow of electrons. Do not trade opposite for parallel or identical.

q: When an electric current is passed through substances, it can produce _____ main effects.
e: Cathode rays go in straight lines, bend in electric or magnetic fields, ionize gas, and make fluorescence. When an electric current is passed through substances, it can produce three main effects. Two or four is not this quantity.

q: The heating effect of current is utilized in electrical appliances such as the _____.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. The heating effect of current is utilized in electrical appliances such as the electric iron. Electric motor or electro-plating tank is not this quantity.

q: The chemical effect of current is used in charging batteries, purifying metals, and _____.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. The chemical effect of current is used in charging batteries, purifying metals, and electro-plating. Electric bells or magnetic relays is not this quantity.

q: The magnetic effect of current is used in making _____.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. The magnetic effect of current is used in making electromagnets. Do not trade electromagnets for fuses or capacitors.

q: The magnitude of the charge of a single electron is _____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The magnitude of the charge of a single electron is 1.6 × 10^-19 C. 1.6 × 10^-18 C or 1.6 × 10^-20 C is a different relation from 1.6 × 10^-19 C.

q: According to Ohm's law, at a constant temperature, the current flowing through a conductor is _____ to the potential difference across it.
e: Ohm's law: V = IR for a metal at steady temperature. According to Ohm's law, at a constant temperature, the current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it. Inversely proportional or unrelated is not this quantity.

q: The mathematical formula representing Ohm's law is _____.
e: Ohm's law: V = IR for a metal at steady temperature. The mathematical formula representing Ohm's law is V = IR. I = (V)/(R) or R = (I)/(V) is a different relation from V = IR.

q: The SI unit of electrical resistance is the _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The SI unit of electrical resistance is the ohm. Ampere or volt is not this quantity.

q: At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor is the _____ of the potential difference between its two ends to the current flowing through it.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor is the ratio of the potential difference between its two ends to the current flowing through it. Do not trade ratio for product or sum.

q: At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor _____ on the potential difference between its ends and the current flowing through it.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor does not depend on the potential difference between its ends and the current flowing through it. Strongly depends or is inversely dependent is not this quantity.

q: At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor is directly proportional to its _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor is directly proportional to its length. Do not trade length for cross-sectional area or volume.

q: At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor is inversely proportional to its _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. At a given temperature, the resistance of a conductor is inversely proportional to its cross-sectional area. Length or resistivity is not this quantity.

q: The formula relating resistance $R$, resistivity $\rho$, length $l$, and cross-sectional area $A$ is _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The formula relating resistance R, resistivity ρ, length l, and cross-sectional area A is R = ρ (l)/(A). R = ρ (A)/(l) or R = (ρ)/(lA) is a different relation from R = ρ (l)/(A).

q: Resistivity of a conductor is defined as the resistance of a conductor having _____ cross-sectional area and one unit length.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. Resistivity of a conductor is defined as the resistance of a conductor having one unit cross-sectional area and one unit length. Do not trade one unit for two unit or half unit.

q: The SI unit of resistivity is the _____.
e: Resistivity ρ is the material constant in R = ρl/A. Its SI unit is ohm metre. The SI unit of resistivity is the ohm metre. Do not trade ohm metre for ohm per metre or ohm metre squared.

q: If the length or the cross-sectional area of a substance changes, its resistance will change, but its _____ remains the same.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. If the length or the cross-sectional area of a substance changes, its resistance will change, but its resistivity remains the same. Conductance or current is not this quantity.

q: The resistance of metals _____ with increasing temperature.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The resistance of metals decreases with increasing temperature. Increases or remains constant is not this quantity.

q: The resistance of carbon (a non-metal) and semiconductors _____ with increasing temperature.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The resistance of carbon (a non-metal) and semiconductors decreases with increasing temperature. Increases or fluctuates randomly is not this quantity.

q: The formula relating the resistance $R_t$ at temperature $t$ to the resistance $R_0$ at $0^{\circ}\text{C}$ is _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The formula relating the resistance R_t at temperature t to the resistance R_0 at 0°C is R_t = R_0(1 + α t). R_t = R_0(1 - α t) or R_t = R_0 + α t is a different relation from R_t = R_0(1 + α t).

q: The unit of the temperature coefficient of resistance $\alpha$ is _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The unit of the temperature coefficient of resistance α is °C⁻¹. Ω°c or ω^-1 is not this quantity.

q: According to Table 10.1, the resistivity of copper at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$ is _____.
e: Resistivity ρ is the material constant in R = ρl/A. Its SI unit is ohm metre. According to Table 10.1, the resistivity of copper at 20°C is 1.72 × 10^-8 Ω m. 2.82 × 10^-8 Ω m or 1.62 × 10^-8 Ω m is a different relation from 1.72 × 10^-8 Ω m.

q: According to Table 10.1, the resistivity of silver at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$ is _____.
e: Resistivity ρ is the material constant in R = ρl/A. Its SI unit is ohm metre. According to Table 10.1, the resistivity of silver at 20°C is 1.62 × 10^-8 Ω m. 1.72 × 10^-8 Ω m or 5.50 × 10^-8 Ω m is a different relation from 1.62 × 10^-8 Ω m.

q: The temperature coefficient of resistance for carbon (graphite) has a _____ value.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The temperature coefficient of resistance for carbon (graphite) has a negative value. Positive or zero is not this quantity.

q: According to Table 10.1, the resistivity of tungsten at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$ is _____.
e: Resistivity ρ is the material constant in R = ρl/A. Its SI unit is ohm metre. According to Table 10.1, the resistivity of tungsten at 20°C is 5.50 × 10^-8 Ω m. 4.8 × 10^-8 Ω m or 9.80 × 10^-8 Ω m is a different relation from 5.50 × 10^-8 Ω m.

q: A resistor is an electrical device which is used to _____ the electric current flowing in a circuit.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. A resistor is an electrical device which is used to control the electric current flowing in a circuit. Do not trade control for amplify or generate.

q: There are _____ main types of resistors.
e: There are two main types of resistors. One or three is not this quantity.

q: A rheostat is an example of a _____ resistor.
e: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to change the potential difference. A rheostat is an example of a variable resistor. Fixed or superconducting is not this quantity.

q: When the resistance value of a variable resistor is increased while the potential difference is kept constant, the electric current passing through it will _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. When the resistance value of a variable resistor is increased while the potential difference is kept constant, the electric current passing through it will decrease. Increase or remain the same is not this quantity.

q: If the potential difference across a variable resistor is kept constant, the current is _____ to the resistance.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. If the potential difference across a variable resistor is kept constant, the current is inversely proportional to the resistance. Do not trade inversely proportional for directly proportional or exponentially proportional.

q: Resistors are said to be connected in series if the _____ flows through each resistor.
e: Resistors are said to be connected in series if the same current flows through each resistor. Same potential difference or different current is not this quantity.

q: For resistors connected in series, the total potential difference $V$ is equal to _____.
e: For resistors connected in series, the total potential difference V is equal to V_1 + V_2 + V_3. V_1 × V_2 × V_3 or (1)/(V_1) + (1)/(V_2) + (1)/(V_3) is a different relation from V_1 + V_2 + V_3.

q: The equivalent resistance $R$ of resistors connected in series is equal to the _____ of the individual resistances.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The equivalent resistance R of resistors connected in series is equal to the sum of the individual resistances. Product or reciprocal sum is not this quantity.

q: Resistors are said to be connected in parallel if the _____ appears across each and every resistor.
e: Resistors are said to be connected in parallel if the same potential difference appears across each and every resistor. Do not trade same potential difference for same current or different potential difference.

q: For resistors connected in parallel, the total current $I$ is equal to _____.
e: For resistors connected in parallel, the total current I is equal to I_1 + I_2 + I_3. I_1 × I_2 × I_3 or (1)/(I_1) + (1)/(I_2) + (1)/(I_3) is a different relation from I_1 + I_2 + I_3.

q: The reciprocal of the equivalent resistance of resistors connected in parallel is equal to the _____ of the reciprocal of the individual resistances.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The reciprocal of the equivalent resistance of resistors connected in parallel is equal to the sum of the reciprocal of the individual resistances. Do not trade sum for product or difference.

q: When a parallel combination of two resistors having different resistances is connected to a battery, the resistor with _____ resistance will draw a greater current.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. When a parallel combination of two resistors having different resistances is connected to a battery, the resistor with smaller resistance will draw a greater current. Larger or equal is not this quantity.

q: The equivalent resistance of three $6 \Omega$ resistors connected in series is _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The equivalent resistance of three 6 Ω resistors connected in series is 18 Ω. Do not trade 18 Ω for 2 Ω or 6 Ω.

q: The equivalent resistance of three $6 \Omega$ resistors connected in parallel is _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The equivalent resistance of three 6 Ω resistors connected in parallel is 2 Ω. 18 ω or 3 ω is not this quantity.

q: The equivalent resistance of two $6 \Omega$ resistors connected in parallel is _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The equivalent resistance of two 6 Ω resistors connected in parallel is 3 Ω. 12 ω or 6 ω is not this quantity.

q: The magnetic effect of an electric current was discovered by _____ in 1820.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. The magnetic effect of an electric current was discovered by Oersted in 1820. Do not trade Oersted for Ampere or Faraday.

q: According to the right-hand rule, if the thumb points along the wire in the direction of the current, the direction of the fingers will give the direction of the _____.
e: Point fingers along A, curl them toward B, and the thumb gives A × B. According to the right-hand rule, if the thumb points along the wire in the direction of the current, the direction of the fingers will give the direction of the magnetic field. Electric field or force is not this quantity.

q: The magnetic lines of force around a straight wire carrying a current are _____.
e: The magnetic lines of force around a straight wire carrying a current are closed circular loops. Straight parallel lines or elliptical loops is not this quantity.

q: The magnetic lines of force around a current-carrying wire are in a plane _____ to the wire.
e: The magnetic lines of force around a current-carrying wire are in a plane perpendicular to the wire. Do not trade perpendicular for parallel or at a 45-degree angle.

q: If the current flowing through a wire is reversed, the direction of the magnetic field will be _____.
e: If the current flowing through a wire is reversed, the direction of the magnetic field will be randomized. Unchanged or reversed is not this quantity.

q: A solenoid is a _____ coil of wire.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. A solenoid is a cylindrical coil of wire. Do not trade cylindrical for rectangular or spherical.

q: The magnetic field of a solenoid is identical with that of a _____.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. The magnetic field of a solenoid is identical with that of a bar magnet. Do not trade bar magnet for horseshoe magnet or ring magnet.

q: When viewing one end of a solenoid, if the current is seen flowing in a clockwise direction, that end will be a _____ pole.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. When viewing one end of a solenoid, if the current is seen flowing in a clockwise direction, that end will be a south pole. Do not trade south for north or neutral.

q: When viewing one end of a solenoid, if the current is seen flowing in an anticlockwise direction, that end will be a _____ pole.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. When viewing one end of a solenoid, if the current is seen flowing in an anticlockwise direction, that end will be a north pole. Do not trade north for south or neutral.

q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the forefinger points in the direction of the _____.
e: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field. Do not trade magnetic field for electric current or motion.

q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the second finger points in the direction of the _____.
e: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the second finger points in the direction of the electric current. Do not trade electric current for magnetic field or force.

q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the thumb points in the direction of the _____.
e: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the thumb points in the direction of the motion or force. Magnetic field or electric current is not this quantity.

q: When a charged particle moves across a magnetic field, the force acting on that particle is perpendicular to both _____ and _____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. When a charged particle moves across a magnetic field, the force acting on that particle is perpendicular to both B and v and _____. Do not trade B and v for E and I or F and I.

q: If a negatively charged particle moves across a magnetic field, the force acting on it will be in the _____ direction compared to a positively charged particle.
e: Thomson showed cathode rays are negative. The particle was later named the electron. If a negatively charged particle moves across a magnetic field, the force acting on it will be in the opposite direction compared to a positively charged particle. Do not trade opposite for same or perpendicular.

q: A solenoid can be used in an electrical device such as an electric motor that converts electrical energy into _____ energy.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. A solenoid can be used in an electrical device such as an electric motor that converts electrical energy into mechanical energy. Do not trade mechanical for chemical or thermal.

q: The best method of making a magnet is to use the _____ of an electric current.
e: Current is charge per second. Conventional current is opposite to electron drift. The best method of making a magnet is to use the magnetic effect of an electric current. Heating effect or chemical effect is not this quantity.

q: When a large current flows through a solenoid with a steel bar placed inside, the steel bar becomes a _____ magnet.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. When a large current flows through a solenoid with a steel bar placed inside, the steel bar becomes a permanent magnet. Temporary or electromagnetic is not this quantity.

q: A soft iron core surrounded by a coil of wire, which acts as a magnet when a current flows, is called a(n) _____.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. A soft iron core surrounded by a coil of wire, which acts as a magnet when a current flows, is called a(n) electromagnet. Do not trade electromagnet for permanent magnet or galvanometer.

q: An electromagnet made with a soft iron core is demagnetized when the _____.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. An electromagnet made with a soft iron core is demagnetized when the voltage increases. Do not trade voltage increases for current stops or coil is heated.

q: Increasing the current in an electromagnet will create a _____ magnetic field strength.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. Increasing the current in an electromagnet will create a stronger magnetic field strength. Do not trade stronger for weaker or fluctuating.

q: Reversing the direction of current in an electromagnet will reverse the _____ of the magnetic field.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. Reversing the direction of current in an electromagnet will reverse the direction of the magnetic field. Do not trade direction for strength or shape.

q: In an electric bell, the soft iron armature is mounted on a _____.
e: An electromagnet drives bells, relays, and motors. In an electric bell, the soft iron armature is mounted on a spring. Screw or gong is not this quantity.

q: In an electric bell, when the switch is pressed, the electromagnets attract the armature and the _____ strikes the gong.
e: An electromagnet drives bells, relays, and motors. In an electric bell, when the switch is pressed, the electromagnets attract the armature and the hammer strikes the gong. Spring or contact plate is not this quantity.

q: In an electric bell, the current stops when the metal plate and the end of the _____ are separated.
e: An electromagnet drives bells, relays, and motors. In an electric bell, the current stops when the metal plate and the end of the screw are separated. Hammer or spring is not this quantity.

q: A circuit breaker is designed to switch off the current in a circuit when an _____ current flows.
e: A circuit breaker is designed to switch off the current in a circuit when an excessive current flows. Do not trade excessive for insufficient or alternating.

q: In a circuit breaker, the _____ will attract the iron armature if the current is large, thus breaking the circuit.
e: In a circuit breaker, the electromagnet will attract the iron armature if the current is large, thus breaking the circuit. Spring or copper strip is not this quantity.

q: Electric bells, magnetic relays, and electric motors are all applications of _____.
e: An electromagnet drives bells, relays, and motors. Electric bells, magnetic relays, and electric motors are all applications of electromagnets. Heating effect or chemical effect is not this quantity.

q: The heating effect of current is utilized in electrical appliances such as electric stove, electric iron, and _____.
e: Current can heat a wire, drive electrolysis, or magnetize a core. Those three effects are used in lamps, plating, and electromagnets. The heating effect of current is utilized in electrical appliances such as electric stove, electric iron, and immersion heater. Do not trade immersion heater for electric motor or magnetic relay.

q: A temporary magnet is also commonly known as a(n) _____.
e: A temporary magnet is also commonly known as a(n) electromagnet. Do not trade electromagnet for permanent magnet or solenoid.

q: An ammeter is a device used for measuring _____.
e: An ammeter is a device used for measuring current. Potential difference or resistance is not this quantity.

q: A voltmeter is a device used for measuring _____.
e: A voltmeter is a device used for measuring potential difference. Do not trade potential difference for current or resistance.

q: Ammeters and voltmeters are constructed based on the principle of a _____.
e: Superposition: the resultant at a point is the sum of the individual displacements. Ammeters and voltmeters are constructed based on the principle of a moving coil galvanometer. Do not trade moving coil galvanometer for solenoid or rheostat.

q: A moving coil galvanometer is a sensitive electromagnetic device which can measure low currents even of the order of a few _____.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. A moving coil galvanometer is a sensitive electromagnetic device which can measure low currents even of the order of a few microamperes. Do not trade microamperes for amperes or milliamperes.

q: In a moving coil galvanometer, the coil is suspended in a uniform _____ magnetic field.
e: In a moving coil galvanometer, the coil is suspended in a uniform radial magnetic field. Do not trade radial for linear or circular.

q: A cylindrical soft iron core is positioned inside the galvanometer coil to improve the strength of the magnetic field and to make the field _____.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. A cylindrical soft iron core is positioned inside the galvanometer coil to improve the strength of the magnetic field and to make the field radial. Uniform or parallel is not this quantity.

q: The spring in a moving coil galvanometer is used to produce a _____ which balances the magnetic torque.
e: Torque is r × F, a cross product, so it is a vector. The spring in a moving coil galvanometer is used to produce a counter torque which balances the magnetic torque. Do not trade counter torque for magnetic field or potential difference.

q: The principle of function of a moving coil galvanometer is that the current-carrying coil when placed in an external magnetic field experiences _____.
e: Superposition: the resultant at a point is the sum of the individual displacements. The principle of function of a moving coil galvanometer is that the current-carrying coil when placed in an external magnetic field experiences magnetic torque. Chemical reaction or heating effect is not this quantity.

q: The angle through which the galvanometer coil is deflected is proportional to the _____ of current in the coil.
e: The angle through which the galvanometer coil is deflected is proportional to the magnitude of current in the coil. Do not trade magnitude for square or reciprocal.

q: A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting it in parallel with a wire of low resistance called _____ resistance.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting it in parallel with a wire of low resistance called shunt resistance. Multiplier or series is not this quantity.

q: The formula for calculating the shunt resistance $r$ is _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The formula for calculating the shunt resistance r is r = (i)/(I - i) R_G. r = (I - i)/(i) R_G or r = i(I - i) R_G is a different relation from r = (i)/(I - i) R_G.

q: An ammeter is a _____ resistance device.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. An ammeter is a low resistance device. High or infinite is not this quantity.

q: An ammeter is connected in _____ with the circuit component.
e: An ammeter is connected in series with the circuit component. Parallel or isolation is not this quantity.

q: A galvanometer is converted into a voltmeter by connecting it in series with a _____ resistance resistor.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. A galvanometer is converted into a voltmeter by connecting it in series with a high resistance resistor. Do not trade high for low or shunt.

q: The formula for calculating the multiplier resistance $R$ for a voltmeter is _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The formula for calculating the multiplier resistance R for a voltmeter is R = (V)/(i) - R_G. R = (V)/(i) + R_G or R = V · i - R_G is a different relation from R = (V)/(i) - R_G.

q: A voltmeter is a _____ resistance device.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. A voltmeter is a high resistance device. Low or zero is not this quantity.

q: A voltmeter is connected in _____ with the circuit component.
e: A voltmeter is connected in parallel with the circuit component. Series or isolation is not this quantity.

q: The moving coil galvanometer coil is made up of many turns of fine _____ wire.
e: The moving coil galvanometer coil is made up of many turns of fine copper wire. Do not trade copper for aluminum or tungsten.

q: It is necessary for the shunt of an ammeter to have a very low resistance so that it can _____.
a: measure large currents without affecting the circuit
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. It is necessary for the shunt of an ammeter to have a very low resistance so that it can measure large currents without affecting the circuit. Do not trade measure large currents without affecting the circuit for increase the voltage drop or act as a fuse.

q: To convert a galvanometer into a voltmeter reading up to a higher voltage, the value of the multiplier resistance must be _____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. To convert a galvanometer into a voltmeter reading up to a higher voltage, the value of the multiplier resistance must be increased. Do not trade increased for decreased or kept the same.
